🔴 **Tests vanish or the run hangs when a worker fails to start** The unit already handed to a worker that dies before finishing startup is never returned or reported (in the worker-exit handler at `packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:406-430`) after it is dequeued, so those tests produce no result and, when the unit is a setup, the run can wait forever. Impact: A worker that fails to boot makes its assigned tests disappear from the report, and if that worker was holding a setup task the entire run deadlocks and never finishes.
How the pending unit is orphaned on init failure When a target first needs a worker, `nextDispatch` spawns one in state `initializing` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:196-197`) and `dispatch` immediately pops a unit from the queue via `takeUnit` (which `shift()`s it off `setupQueue`/`fileQueue`, `packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:222-223`) and stores it on `slot.pendingUnit` because the slot is not yet `idle` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:172-173`). The unit is now off the queue and only referenced by `slot.pendingUnit`. If that worker exits before emitting `ready` (config/digest error, driver resolve throw, spawn failure), `onExit` runs with `slot.dispatched === undefined`, so it only increments `initFailures` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:425-428`) and calls `removeSlot(slot)`. It never re-queues `slot.pendingUnit`, never emits skip/crash results for its pairs, and never calls `completeUnit`. Consequences: - File unit: its tests get no `ResultRecord` at all — silently missing from the report. - Setup unit: `completeUnit` is never called, so `pendingSetups` stays > 0. `peekUnit` then returns `undefined` for that target (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:213`), so no file units dispatch and no worker respawns (nothing to dispatch). Meanwhile `isDone` is false because `fileQueue.length > 0` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:151-157`), so the main loop awaits `wake` (`packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts:117-119`) with no pending worker to ever wake it — a permanent hang. `MAX_INIT_FAILURES` is never reached because respawning requires a peekable unit.
Prompt for agents ``` In ParallelScheduler.onExit (packages/e2e/src/run/scheduler.ts around lines 406-430), a worker that exits before sending 'ready' can be holding a unit in slot.pendingUnit. That unit was already removed from the target's setupQueue/fileQueue by takeUnit, but onExit never puts it back, never emits results for its pairs, and never calls completeUnit. For a file unit this silently drops all its tests from the report; for a setup unit it leaves pendingSetups > 0, which blocks all file units for that target (peekUnit returns undefined) and prevents respawn, so the run loop awaits wake forever and deadlocks (MAX_INIT_FAILURES is never reached). Fix approach: in onExit, before/alongside the initFailures handling, check slot.pendingUnit. If a pending unit exists on a worker that exited without becoming ready, either (a) re-queue it to the front of the appropriate queue (setupQueue or fileQueue) so it can be retried/failed by the normal path, or (b) treat it like a crashed unit — synthesize infrastructure-unavailable results for its pairs and call completeUnit(state, pendingUnit) so pendingSetups is decremented. Whichever is chosen, ensure pendingSetups accounting stays correct and that failTarget draining also accounts for any pending unit. Also confirm the same handling covers the case where the worker was interrupted while still initializing. ```

🟡 **Configuration guide states the wrong default for report output selection** The configuration guide lists the default set of report outputs as list-only (`['list']` at `fern/docs/pages/configuration.mdx:136`), but the runner actually defaults to list plus html, so readers are told the wrong out-of-the-box behavior. Impact: A reader relying on the Configuration page will believe html is not enabled by default, contradicting the reference page and the Running-tests page and the runner itself.
Where the default is actually set In `packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:174` the resolved default is `['list', 'html']`. The reference page `fern/docs/pages/reference/config.mdx:57` correctly documents `['list', 'html']`, and `fern/docs/pages/running-tests.mdx:150` explicitly states "`html` is part of the default `reporters` value". Only `fern/docs/pages/configuration.mdx:136` disagrees, listing the default as `['list']` and also dropping `html` from the type column.
```suggestion | `reporters` | `('list' \| 'json' \| 'html')[]` | `['list', 'html']` | Select with `--reporter`; `.e2e/report.json` is written either way | ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Same-origin content embedded in blank or inline-HTML frames disappears from what the agent can see** Child frames are now dropped from the observation when their address's origin is not listed (`isAllowedFrameOrigin(frame.url(), ...)` at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:682`), but frames created without navigation report an address like `about:blank` or `about:srcdoc` whose origin is treated as none, so genuinely same-origin app content inside them is skipped. Impact: On some real pages the agent can no longer read or act on UI that lives inside inline or not-yet-navigated frames, causing legitimate targets to become invisible.
Why about:blank/srcdoc frames fall through the origin gate Before this PR, `captureDocument` descended into every reachable child frame within the depth budget. The new guard at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:682` requires `new URL(frame.url()).origin` to be a member of `allowedOrigins` (`isAllowedFrameOrigin` at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:738-744`). A frame written via `srcdoc` or one that has not committed a navigation reports its URL as `about:srcdoc` / `about:blank`; `new URL('about:blank').origin` evaluates to the string `"null"`, which is never in `allowedOrigins`, so the frame is excluded even though the browser considers it same-origin with the parent document. This is a behavior change from unconditional capture, and such frames can carry real, actionable application UI (rich-text editors, some consent/embed widgets). It is distinct from the intended goal of excluding third-party ad/tracker frames.
Prompt for agents ``` The new frame-origin gate in captureDocument (packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:682, isAllowedFrameOrigin at :738) excludes any child frame whose committed URL is not in allowedOrigins. This correctly filters third-party frames, but it also excludes same-origin frames that report a non-http URL such as about:blank or about:srcdoc (frames written via srcdoc or not yet navigated), because new URL('about:blank').origin is the string 'null'. Those frames are same-origin with the parent and can contain real application UI the agent must read and act on. Consider treating about:blank/about:srcdoc frames as same-origin with their parent document (e.g. allow the frame when its URL is about:blank/about:srcdoc/empty, or resolve the effective origin from the owning document) so legitimately embedded same-origin content is still captured, while still excluding cross-origin ad/tracker frames. ```

🟡 **A failed screenshot turns an optional vision request into a whole-step failure** When a vision request asks for pixels, a failed screenshot capture (`this.capturePixels(...)` at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:636`) is rethrown instead of being swallowed, so a call that should quietly continue with the tree alone fails outright. Impact: A momentary screenshot problem on a vision assert/tap makes the whole test step fail, even though it was designed to keep working without the picture.
Why the degradation path is bypassed The vision tier is built so pixel evidence "degrades rather than failing a call": the runner only degrades when the driver returns an observation whose `pixels` field is absent (see `recordPixels`/`degradeVision` in `packages/e2e/src/agent/invocation.ts:239-254`, which map an absent image to `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`). `spec/09-drivers.md` states the driver contract directly: "A driver that cannot capture pixels omits them rather than failing the observation." In `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:635-637`, `capturePixels` is awaited inside the observation's `try` block, and the `catch` at `:638-641` only disposes the handle generation and rethrows. `capturePixels` catches only the mask `count()` calls (`:674`), not `page.screenshot(...)` (`:676`). So if the screenshot itself rejects — a timeout under load, or a page that closes/navigates mid-capture — the error propagates out of `observe()` and fails the entire agent step, rather than returning an observation with `pixels` omitted and letting the runner record a withheld/degraded vision step. This is the one place that can produce a hard failure for what the design and spec require to be a graceful, tree-only fallback.
Prompt for agents ``` In PlaywrightSession.observe (packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts), the optional pixel capture at line 636 (capturePixels) is awaited inside the try block whose catch simply rethrows, so any failure of page.screenshot inside capturePixels fails the entire observation. This contradicts the driver-1 contract in spec/09-drivers.md ('A driver that cannot capture pixels omits them rather than failing the observation') and the vision degradation design, which relies on the driver returning an Observation with pixels omitted so the runner can record the step as degraded (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY) and continue tree-only. Make a capture failure leave capturedPixels undefined instead of propagating, so the semantic tree is still returned. Be careful to still propagate genuine cancellation/abort of the operation (do not swallow a cancelled/aborted signal into a silent tree-only success); only non-cancellation capture errors should degrade to omitting pixels. ```

🟨 **Committed cache regexp can cause catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) during replay** A `cache-1` entry is treated as untrusted repository input, and its locator/query text patterns may be regular expressions (`packages/e2e/src/cache/locator.ts:179-202`, `packages/e2e/src/cache/entry.ts:270-278`). Validation only enforces a 1,024-byte source cap, mutual exclusion of `u`/`v`, and canonical flag order — it does not bound pattern complexity or evaluation time. On a cache hit these patterns are evaluated inline while resolving the stored locator (`packages/e2e/src/agent/locate-cache.ts:121` via `engine.resolveAll`), where the driver compiles and runs the regexp against page text. A crafted pattern well under 1 KiB (e.g. nested quantifiers) can trigger catastrophic backtracking and hang the runner/driver process, so a malicious committed or restored cache entry becomes a denial-of-service vector. The PR itself notes the spec's interruptible-worker regexp evaluation is not implemented and evaluation runs inline. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Screenshot resizing can stall an observation with no time limit or cancellation** The screenshot resize is run as a browser evaluation (`page.evaluate(resizeImageFunction, ...)` at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:779`) with no timeout and no link to the operation's cancellation signal, unlike the screenshot capture right before it which is bounded, so a slow or unresponsive scratch page holds the observation open indefinitely. Impact: A single stuck resize can hang the whole step past its budget with no way to cancel it, rather than degrading to a full-scale image.
Why the resize step is unbounded while capture is bounded In `packages/e2e/src/playwright/observe.ts:47-54` the `page.screenshot(...)` call is capped by `Math.max(1, Math.min(operation.timeoutMs, PIXEL_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS))`. The new resize step (`downscale` at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/observe.ts:83-94` calling the `resize` callback, which is `this.resizeImage` at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:777-781`) receives neither `operation.timeoutMs` nor `operation.signal`. `page.evaluate` has no implicit timeout and the scratch context never sets one (`packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:786` omits the `setDefaultTimeout` the main context gets at line 161). The pixel-capture promise in `observe()` is guarded only by `.catch(() => undefined)`, which handles rejection but not a hang; the invocation deadline (`checkDeadline`) is only evaluated between phases, so an in-flight resize is never interrupted. Spec 09-drivers.md states a driver operation MUST observe both `AbortSignal` and `timeoutMs`. Likelihood is low (image decode/encode rarely hangs), hence non-severe.
Prompt for agents ``` The resize step in PlaywrightSession.resizeImage (packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts) runs page.evaluate on the scratch page with no timeout and no tie to the observation operation's AbortSignal, unlike capturePixels' screenshot call which is bounded by operation.timeoutMs/PIXEL_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS. Thread the OperationContext (or at least a timeout and the abort signal) through capturePixels' resize callback into resizeImage, and wrap the page.evaluate in a bounded race (e.g. the existing withTimeout helper used elsewhere in session.ts) so a stuck scratch-page evaluation rejects and downscale falls back to full-scale bytes instead of hanging the observation. Ensure cancellation via operation.signal is also observed, per spec 09-drivers.md which requires driver operations to observe both AbortSignal and timeoutMs. ```
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Scratch browser context is leaked when its page closes unexpectedly** When the scratch page has closed (for example after a browser page crash) a brand-new browser context is created and stored (`this.scratchContext = context` at `packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:787`) without first closing the previous scratch context, so the old context is orphaned and only the newest one is released at session close. Impact: Repeated scratch-page crashes during a long-running session accumulate abandoned browser contexts that stay open until the browser itself is torn down.
How the orphaned context arises `scratchPage()` (`packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:783-791`) reuses the scratch page only when `existing !== null && !existing.isClosed()`. If the page exists but is closed, it falls through and calls `this.browser.newContext(...)`, overwriting `this.scratchContext` with the new context while the old `BrowserContext` (still holding the closed page) is never closed. `close()` (`packages/e2e/src/playwright/session.ts:797`) only closes the current `this.scratchContext`, so every superseded context leaks for the lifetime of the shared, pool-owned browser. Edge-case (requires the scratch page to close/crash mid-session), hence non-severe.
```suggestion private async scratchPage(): Promise { const existing = this.scratch; if (existing !== null && !existing.isClosed()) return existing; await this.scratchContext?.close().catch(() => undefined); this.scratchContext = null; this.scratch = null; const context = await this.browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1, height: 1 } }); this.scratchContext = context; const page = await context.newPage(); this.scratch = page; return page; } ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

Fixed in 521f743 — and this was a plain mistake, not a judgement call: the `page.screenshot` immediately before it is bounded by `Math.min(operation.timeoutMs, PIXEL_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS)`, and I left the resize right next to it unbounded.

Worse than the hang itself, it falsified the property this feature was designed around. I claimed "a resizer that fails returns full-scale bytes, so a broken resize costs tokens and never correctness" — but `.catch(() => undefined)` only covers a rejection, so that guarantee held only for failures that announced themselves. A hang bypassed it entirely.

Now bounded by `Math.min(operation.timeoutMs, RESIZE_TIMEOUT_MS)` (5 s) via the existing `withTimeout`, with `void evaluation.catch(...)` so a late settle cannot become an unhandled rejection. Added a unit test for the fallback: a rejecting resizer returns the original bytes, which is what keeps the reported geometry consistent with what was actually sent.

On the `AbortSignal` half of your point: I added `checkOperation(operation)` at entry, but did not race the signal in flight, because no operation in this driver does. `page.screenshot` in `capturePixels` observes `timeoutMs` only, and `guard()` checks cancellation at entry and cannot interrupt work already dispatched. So in-flight signal observation is a real gap against spec 09-drivers.md — it just isn't specific to this path, and fixing it only here would make the resize the one operation with different semantics. Worth doing uniformly across the driver rather than as a rider on this PR.

Fixed in 521f743, taking your suggested shape: the spent context is closed and both fields cleared before a replacement is built.

Correct diagnosis — `scratchPage` reused the page only while it was open, then wrote a fresh context over `this.scratchContext`, so the old one was unreachable and `close()` only ever released the newest. Since the browser is pool-owned and outlives the session, a crash loop would have accumulated contexts for the life of the pool rather than the life of the session, which is the part that makes it worth fixing despite being an edge case.

🔴 **Pressing a named key on a phone types the key's name into the field instead** A key press from a locator is sent to the device as literal text (`type({ text: action.key })` at `packages/e2e/src/agent-device/actions.ts:181`) instead of the character that key produces, so pressing Enter inserts the word "Enter" into the field and the step still reports success. Impact: Mobile tests that submit a form or press a named key silently corrupt the field's contents and pass anyway.
Why the key name reaches the app verbatim `keys.ts` exists precisely to avoid this: `keyToText` maps `Enter` to `\r`, `Backspace` to `\^H`, and returns `undefined` for a key the platform cannot express, and `requireKeyText` (`packages/e2e/src/agent-device/actions.ts:39-45`) turns that into `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. The agent path uses it (`packages/e2e/src/agent-device/session.ts:451`), but the `LocatorAction` path in `performAction` does not: `locator.press('Enter')` builds `{ kind: 'press', key: 'Enter' }` (`packages/e2e/src/locator/screen.ts:237`) and `actions.ts:181` forwards `action.key` straight to `interactions.type`. Multi-character key names such as `Enter`, `Tab`, `ArrowDown`, or `F13` are therefore typed as words, and an unsupported key never fails.
```suggestion await withDeadline( client.interactions.type({ platform: scope.platform, text: requireKeyText(action.key, scope.platform), }), operation, 'press', ); ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔴 **Retries for a moved element stop working for drivers loaded outside the runner** The new structural recognition of a driver failure is used only when classifying errors for the report (`asDriverError` at `packages/e2e/src/internal/errors.ts:61-67`) and not where the runner decides whether an operation may be retried, so a recoverable "the element moved" failure from such a driver becomes an immediate test failure. Impact: Tests against a third-party or mobile driver fail with "element not found" instead of simply re-looking for the element.
Where the class-based check still remains The PR's premise is that a driver loaded through a different module registry throws a `DriverError` that is a different class, so `instanceof` misses it. `errors.ts` was converted to structural detection, but `packages/e2e/src/locator/engine.ts` still gates on the class: - `engine.ts:100` — `cause instanceof DriverError && cause.retryable` decides whether a retryable `NODE_STALE` / `FRAME_NOT_FOUND` resolve is retried within the deadline; - `engine.ts:173` — decides whether a stale read during polling is treated as "zero matches" instead of a hard error; - `engine.ts:196-202` — decides whether a stale `perform` re-resolves. The mobile driver invalidates its snapshot on every mutation and reports `NODE_STALE` with `retryable: true` (`packages/e2e/src/agent-device/session.ts:265-277`), which is exactly the case these loops exist for. With the class check failing, the error falls through to `translateDriverError` and surfaces as `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` / `ACTION_FAILED`.
Prompt for agents ``` The cross-realm DriverError problem was only fixed in internal/errors.ts. src/locator/engine.ts still uses `cause instanceof DriverError` in three places that control retry behaviour: resolveOnce (retryable resolve failures), tryRead (NODE_STALE treated as zero matches), and perform (stale re-resolve). A DriverError thrown by a driver loaded through another module registry will not match, so retryable staleness — which the agent-device driver produces after every mutation — turns into an immediate test failure. Export a shared structural predicate (code in the closed driver-1 code set plus the retryable flag) from internal/errors.ts and use it in engine.ts instead of instanceof, so retryability and NODE_STALE detection work for foreign instances too. ```
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Every device call permanently attaches a listener to the test's cancellation signal** The cancellation listener registered for one backend call is never detached when that call finishes (`addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true })` at `packages/e2e/src/agent-device/support.ts:131`), so listeners pile up on the test's signal for the whole test. Impact: Long mobile tests accumulate hundreds of stale listeners, producing Node max-listener warnings and holding memory until the test ends.
Lifetime mismatch between the guard promise and the signal `withDeadline` is called for every single daemon round trip (snapshot, click, fill, scroll, screenshot, …) and receives the attempt-scoped `operation.signal`, which lives for the entire test. The timer is cleared in `finally` (`packages/e2e/src/agent-device/support.ts:136`) but the abort listener is not removed, and `{ once: true }` only removes it if an abort actually fires. Each listener retains the guard promise's `reject` closure. An `AbortSignal` is an `EventTarget`, and Node emits `MaxListenersExceededWarning` past its default cap, so the leak is also user-visible noise.
```suggestion const onAbort = () => { reject(new DriverError('CANCELLED', `${label} cancelled`, { retryable: false })); }; cleanupAbort = () => operation.signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort); operation.signal.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true }); }); try { return await Promise.race([work, guard]); } finally { if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer); cleanupAbort?.(); } ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **A row can become untargetable by its text when an invisible wrapper carries the same label** A label is passed down to descendants as "already claimed" even when the node holding it was rejected for having no usable position (`labelsForChildren` at `packages/e2e/src/agent-device/snapshot.ts:226-227`), so a genuinely visible row nested inside such a wrapper is denied ownership of its own text and no node matches the label at all. Impact: A visible mobile element can be impossible to find by its text or label, making the test fail as if the element were missing.
Ownership propagation ignores whether the ancestor actually owns the label Ownership is computed as `own !== undefined && rect !== undefined && !ancestorLabels.has(own)` (`packages/e2e/src/agent-device/snapshot.ts:218-220`), i.e. a node with no usable rect never owns its label. But the set handed to the children is built from `own` unconditionally, so an ancestor that failed the geometry check still blocks its descendants. Concretely: a wrapper whose reported rect is zero-sized or inconsistent with the tree (the stale-geometry case this module explicitly handles) carries label `X`; its child has valid geometry and the same label `X`. The wrapper cannot own `X` (no rect) and the child is refused it (`ancestorLabels` contains `X`), so `ownedText`/`ownedLabel` return `undefined` for both and `getByText('X')` resolves to zero matches. Only labels the node actually owns should be added to the set handed down.
```suggestion const boundsForChildren = projected.scrollContainer ? undefined : rect ?? trustedAncestorRect; const labelsForChildren = own === undefined || !owns ? ancestorLabels : new Set([...ancestorLabels, own]); ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟨 **Mobile config with no app URL leaves navigation origin policy effectively empty** When no app URL is configured (the new mobile-only path), `allowedOrigins` defaults to an empty list (`packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:325`) and the app environment silently defaults to `test` (`packages/e2e/src/config/resolve.ts:303-313`). `device.openUrl` and `app.deepLink` then only origin-check `http(s)` URLs (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:214-217`, `packages/e2e/src/run/fixtures.ts:296-303`); every custom-scheme URL is passed through to the device unchecked by design. Combined with a default `test` environment inferred from no host at all, a mobile config can drive arbitrary device URLs with no declared policy and no production guard. *(Refers to lines 300-325)* --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Browser driver can be reported as not installed even after the user installs it** The runner loads the browser driver package by name from inside its own installed copy (`await import(wellKnown.specifier)` at `packages/e2e/src/run/resolve-driver.ts:31`) without declaring that package as an (optional) peer dependency, so under strict dependency layouts the lookup fails and the run stops with an "install it to run this target" error even though the package is installed. Impact: Users on Yarn PnP (and pnpm configured without hoisting) cannot run any web test after following the documented install instructions.
Why the on-demand import needs a declared peer `packages/e2e/package.json` lists `@e2edev/playwright` only under `devDependencies` (workspace link), and there is no `peerDependencies`/`peerDependenciesMeta` entry, even though the changeset (`.changeset/plenty-camels-search.md:11`) and the registry comment (`packages/e2e/src/config/drivers.ts:4-5`) both state the package "is declared as an optional peer dependency". Node resolves the bare specifier relative to the `e2e` package directory. With npm's flat/hoisted `node_modules` this accidentally finds the project-level install (which is what the PR's manual verification exercised). Under Yarn PnP the import is rejected because the dependency is undeclared, and under pnpm it only works via the hidden hoisted store, i.e. by accident. Both cases surface as the `DRIVER_NOT_INSTALLED` branch at `packages/e2e/src/run/resolve-driver.ts:32-38`, telling the user to install something they already installed. Declaring the driver as an optional peer dependency of `e2e` is the standard mechanism here; the release note about changesets escalating both packages to major can be handled with the changeset `onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange` option already present in `.changeset/config.json:12` or by ignoring the peer in versioning, rather than by dropping the declaration.
Prompt for agents ``` The runner dynamically imports the driver package by bare specifier in packages/e2e/src/run/resolve-driver.ts, but packages/e2e/package.json does not declare @e2edev/playwright as a dependency of any kind other than a devDependency. Bare-specifier resolution from inside an installed `e2e` package therefore relies on hoisting: it works with npm's flat node_modules but is rejected under Yarn PnP and is only accidental under pnpm, producing a misleading DRIVER_NOT_INSTALLED error for a user who did install the driver. Both .changeset/plenty-camels-search.md and the comment in packages/e2e/src/config/drivers.ts already claim the package is an optional peer dependency. Add the optional peer declaration (peerDependencies + peerDependenciesMeta.optional) with a range that will not fall out of date, and address the changesets major-escalation concern via config (e.g. onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange, already enabled) or by ignoring the peer bump, instead of by omitting the declaration. ```

🟡 **A driver that fails to set up its backend can be reported as a failed test** A failure while getting the backend ready is run through the generic driver-error translation (`translateDriverError` at `packages/e2e/src/run/runner.ts:354`), which turns several driver error codes into test failures, so a run that never executed a test can exit with the test-failure exit code. Impact: Infrastructure/provisioning problems can be reported to the user and to CI as "a test failed", with no test in the report.

  const deadline = Date.now() + CURSOR_TARGET_TIMEOUT_MS;

🔴 **Sibling ZIP artifacts get destroyed** A trace beside another ZIP makes `redactTraceArchives` rewrite that unrelated artifact. One unreadable sibling causes every ZIP in the directory to be deleted.
Learn more The engine contract defines `stopTrace` as returning one relative path. It does not reserve the path's parent directory for trace segments. Scanning that entire directory therefore includes arbitrary ZIP files produced by the engine or test. Any selected file containing a registered value is rewritten, and one unsupported or malformed ZIP sends every selected file through the deletion branch. **Example:** A custom engine returns `artifacts/trace.zip` and also writes `artifacts/export.zip`. A secret fill makes both files enter redaction. If `export.zip` uses an unsupported compression method, both the trace and the export are deleted. **Recommended fix:** Redact only the path returned by `stopTrace`. If segmented traces are part of the engine contract, extend `stopTrace` to return the complete segment list and update the engine SPI, implementations, types, and changesets together.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Required trace failure passes cleanup** A failed rewrite of a required trace returns successfully from `stopRecording`. The attempt remains passed despite producing no requested trace.
Learn more A configured artifact kind has `required` policy. Finalization failures for that policy set `record.cleanup` to `failed` in [stopRecording](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/b1e3f91f73462196019ef4cc69c79c17888d84e1/packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts#L614-L635 "packages/e2e/src/run/execute.ts:614-635"). This inner catch consumes the rewrite failure before `stopRecording` can apply that contract, even though the trace is deleted and never registered. **Example:** A project configures `artifacts: ['trace']`. One trace entry uses an unsupported ZIP method, so redaction deletes the trace and records `TRACE_WITHHELD`. The test and cleanup still pass, although the explicitly required trace is absent. **Recommended fix:** After recording `TRACE_WITHHELD`, set `record.cleanup = 'failed'` when `this.config.artifacts.get('trace') === 'required'`. Keep best-effort traces non-fatal.

🟡 **Credential text corrupts trace records** A credential matching JSON syntax or trace metadata makes `redact` replace unrelated occurrences. The resulting archive is marked complete but cannot be opened.
Learn more The redactor performs unstructured substring replacement over each complete text member. Trace members contain JSON and newline-delimited JSON, so a credential can equal structural syntax, a property name, or a fixed metadata value unrelated to the fill. The ZIP checksum remains valid after rewriting, but the trace format can become invalid or semantically corrupted. **Example:** With a configured password of `"`, every JSON delimiter in `trace.trace` is replaced by ``. The archive is registered as `complete`, but the trace viewer cannot parse any record. **Recommended fix:** Parse known textual trace formats and redact only string values before reserializing them. For opaque text resources, use a replacement strategy that cannot alter container syntax, and validate rewritten trace records before registering the archive as complete.

Learn more The function promises to translate every rewrite failure into `TRACE_WITHHELD`, but archive discovery is part of that operation. Keeping `readdir` outside the boundary exposes filesystem errors directly. **Example:** If `stopTrace` returns a path whose directory was removed before cleanup, `readdir` throws `ENOENT`. The attempt records the generic classification rather than `TRACE_WITHHELD`. **Recommended fix:** Move archive discovery inside the existing `try`. 🟡 **Linked dependencies lose CommonJS format** A symlinked CommonJS TypeScript dependency makes `asModule` classify its real target as ESM. Node resolves package symlinks before this check, removing `node_modules`. Imports using `require` or `module.exports` then fail.
Learn more Node's default module resolver canonicalizes symlinks before returning a file URL. A dependency installed with a workspace link, `file:` reference, or package-manager link can therefore resolve to a source directory that contains no `node_modules` path segment. This check then treats the dependency's `.ts` files as project files, including relative imports inside that package. A CommonJS package can use TypeScript source with `require`, `exports`, or `module.exports`, so changing its format to ESM breaks loading despite the documented dependency exception. **Example:** A project links `common-helper` from `../common-helper`. Its manifest sets `"type": "commonjs"` and exports `src/index.ts`, which assigns `module.exports`. Importing it from an e2e test resolves to `file:///work/common-helper/src/index.ts`; `asModule` forces `format: 'module'`, and evaluation fails because `module` is unavailable. **Recommended fix:** Track whether resolution remains in the config/test module graph without crossing a package dependency boundary, rather than inferring dependency status from the canonical URL. Preserve the resolver's package classification for bare-package roots and their descendants, including symlinked workspace and `file:` dependencies. Add an integration test with a linked CommonJS package that exports `.ts` source.

🟡 **Plain assertions never unlock cached actions** A plain-value `expect(...)` after `agent.act` never verifies its trace. Only recorded assertions advance verification, so the action remains uncached.
Learn more Plain-value matchers run synchronously and never enter the step recorder. Cache eligibility uses the recorder's last passed verification index, so these matchers cannot confirm a staged action trace. Locator assertions, `web` assertions, locator `waitFor`, `agent.assert`, and `agent.waitFor` are recorded with verification enabled. **Example:** `await agent.act('save'); expect(saved).toBe(true)` leaves the action uncached. Replacing the second line with `await expect(screen.getByText('Saved')).toBeVisible()` verifies the trace. **Recommended fix:** Name only recorded assertion surfaces as verification steps and state that plain-value matchers do not qualify.
```suggestion An entry is written only once a **recorded verification step** after the `act` passes: a locator or `web` assertion, a locator `waitFor`, or an `agent.assert` or `agent.waitFor` judgment. Synchronous assertions on plain values are not recorded and do not verify a trace. A trailing `act` nothing ever checks is never replayed blind. Pair every `agent.act()` with a recorded assertion of its outcome to make it cacheable. ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Screenshot behavior is documented incorrectly** A failed locator `expect` creates no screenshot. `agent.assert` can capture one after either verdict, but evidence can also be omitted.
Learn more Locator expectations only record assertion steps; their implementation has no screenshot capture. The built-in `agent.assert` attempts evidence capture before checking its verdict, so successful assertions can also leave screenshots. It skips evidence when `screenshot: false`, after a secret fill, or when capture fails. **Example:** A failing `expect(screen.getByText('Saved')).toBeVisible()` leaves no screenshot. A passing `agent.assert('Saved is visible')` can leave one. **Recommended fix:** Describe screenshots as `agent.assert` evidence rather than failed-`expect` evidence, and preserve the existing permission and capability conditions.

Learn more A variadic positional after `--` legitimately supports names beginning with a dash. Before this change, `e2e run -- -smoke.e2e.ts` reached collection and selected that file. The new parser rejects the token before loading the project root or checking whether it names an existing test. CLI inputs are a stable public contract under [the stability policy](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/d449f8ef4e80d28d8ccb431dc12f838839194ea2/CONTRIBUTING.md#L124-L148 "CONTRIBUTING.md:124-148"), so removing this accepted form requires a warning and deprecation window. **Example:** A project discovers `-smoke.e2e.ts` at its root. `e2e list -- -smoke.e2e.ts` previously listed it, but now exits 2 before collection. Writing `./-smoke.e2e.ts` works, but existing scripts break without warning. **Recommended fix:** Defer dash-prefixed positional validation until the project root is known. Continue accepting an existing dash-prefixed path, and reject only tokens that do not resolve to an existing entry. If support must be removed, preserve the old form with the required runtime warning and deprecation window.

Learn more The argument parser runs once per positional and throws as soon as it sees the dash-prefixed token. It therefore cannot include later tokens that belong to that option. The diagnostic recommends `pnpm exec e2e run --tag`, which Commander rejects because `smoke` is missing. It must recommend `pnpm exec e2e run --tag smoke`. **Recommended fix:** Validate the completed `files` array after Commander has collected every positional. 🔴 **Negated global regex passes falsely** With `.not.toMatch()` and a global or sticky RegExp, `pollMatcher` can pass on an unchanged matching value. `RegExp.test` advances `lastIndex`, and the next sample reuses that matcher argument without resetting it.
Learn more The value matcher's `toMatch` calls `expected.test(actual)` directly [in the matcher implementation](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/dac07f5f2256b978e7e9c01f5bc312f9e245dc5e/packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts#L122-L133 "packages/e2e/src/expect/values.ts:122-133"). A global or sticky RegExp stores the end of its previous match in `lastIndex`. Polling invokes that matcher repeatedly with the same RegExp object. In a negated poll, the first successful regex match is an assertion failure, but it also advances `lastIndex`; the next identical sample can then fail the regex and satisfy the negation. **Example:** `await expect.poll(() => 'done', { interval: 10 }).not.toMatch(/done/g)` must time out because every sample contains `done`. The first sample matches and advances `lastIndex` to 4. The second sample starts at index 4, reports no match, and the poll passes despite no state change. **Recommended fix:** Reset `lastIndex` before every RegExp match, preferably in `ValueExpectationImpl.toMatch` so synchronous and polled value matchers share stateless semantics. Learn more `Deadline` computes `endsAt` by adding the supplied timeout to `Date.now()` [in its constructor](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/dac07f5f2256b978e7e9c01f5bc312f9e245dc5e/packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts#L5-L19 "packages/e2e/src/internal/time.ts:5-19"). `NaN` makes every expiration comparison false, while `Infinity` remains later than every finite clock value. 🟡 **Released ports can be stolen** After `allocateAppPorts` releases each reservation, another process can claim an assigned port before the app binds it. Concurrent runs then fail startup or readiness on the stolen port.
Learn more The allocator discovers a free port by binding a temporary server. Closing that server returns the port to the operating system before any declared command starts. Nothing reserves the port during engine preparation, collection, or command spawning, so another process can bind it first. This race directly affects the parallel-checkout use case introduced by the change. **Example:** Run A reserves port 43123 and closes its temporary server. Run B binds 43123 before Run A's dev server starts. Run A then gets `EADDRINUSE`, or its readiness probe reaches Run B's process. **Recommended fix:** Avoid a check-then-release allocation contract. Prefer having the spawned app bind port 0 and communicate its actual port back to the runner, or introduce an ownership-preserving handoff supported by the child process. If neither is possible, the API cannot guarantee a free port at command bind time and must not claim concurrent-run isolation.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Localhost allocation checks one family** When `localhost` resolves to IPv6 but the app binds IPv4, `reserve` checks the wrong socket namespace. The allocated port can already be occupied on IPv4, so the app fails startup.
Learn more TCP port availability is scoped by bind address and address family. `net.Server.listen(0, 'localhost')` resolves one address, while the command receives only a number and can bind another address such as `127.0.0.1`. Availability on `::1` does not prove availability on IPv4. **Example:** Another service owns `127.0.0.1:43123`. The reservation binds `::1` and the kernel assigns 43123 because that IPv6 endpoint is free. A dev server configured to bind `127.0.0.1` then fails with `EADDRINUSE`. **Recommended fix:** Define the binding contract for hostnames that resolve to multiple addresses. Resolve all addresses the app may use and ensure the chosen port is available on each required socket namespace, or restrict free-port URLs to numeric loopback addresses and document that the command must bind that exact address.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

The engine-contract release rule requires changesets for all three first-party packages so versions from one release remain aligned. **Example:** The current changeset advances only `@e2edev/e2e`. 🔴 **Cancelled transition still dispatches action** When cancellation reaches `awaitTransition`, its sleep resolves and the abandoned `run` dispatches the action anyway. An unpinned retry can inherit that mutation after `settleInflight` completes.
Learn more The surface tracks the whole `run` promise because agent-device commands cannot be cancelled after dispatch. Here cancellation occurs before dispatch, while `awaitTransition` is waiting. The local `sleep` resolves on abort, so `run` continues into the interaction after the caller already received `CANCELLED`. The promise remains in `inflight`, but that only makes the next attempt wait for the unwanted action to finish. **Example:** A test taps a button that opens a modal, then starts tapping the modal's Submit button. 🔴 **Large downloads exhaust worker memory** A large download makes `readFile` allocate its full size in the worker. The worker can exhaust its heap and crash the run.
Learn more Downloads previously used the streaming `measure` path when no artifact store was configured. Scanning now routes every download through `readFile`, so the peak heap allocation grows with the download size before hashing or scanning begins. Browser downloads have no size bound in this path. **Example:** A test downloads a 1.5 GB database export with no artifact store configured. Registration reads all 1.5 GB into the worker heap, while the expected behavior is to scan and hash the file without retaining the whole export. **Recommended fix:** Scan and hash downloads incrementally. Use a streaming multi-pattern matcher that preserves enough overlap between chunks for the longest ledger form. Buffer the bytes only when an `ArtifactStore` requires them, or revise that store contract to accept a stream.

The run-wide map still includes a required video entry, and `validateEngine` rejects the target before inspecting runnable pairs. That prevents a fully opted-out suite from running on an engine without video support. **Example:** A device engine has no video capability; the command uses `--video`, and the sole selected test declares `{ video: false }`. No video would be started, but preflight raises `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT` instead of running the test. **Recommended fix:** Grade `video` against runnable pairs' resolved plans; keep the run-wide validation for other artifacts and for entry points without per-test options. 🔴 **Provider replay misses replacement browser** When a worker-scope browser drops mid-attempt, `ProviderVideo` keeps recording its original lease after the replacement attaches. Its no-op `pageOpened` cannot start recording the replacement, so the replay omits subsequent test activity.
Learn more A worker-scoped provider holds a browser lease for a worker, but [endpoint](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/d6c6e7178bfba15ebe1be80a91bf92e29c1b7f9f/packages/web/src/provider.ts#L398-L414 "packages/web/src/provider.ts:398-414") replaces that lease when the browser drops. [recorder](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/d6c6e7178bfba15ebe1be80a91bf92e29c1b7f9f/packages/web/src/provider.ts#L472-L501 "packages/web/src/provider.ts:472-501") captures the original lease in the recording's stop callback. After the connection recovers, the attempt keeps using the new browser while its provider recording still belongs to the old one. **Example:** A worker starts a Kernel replay on browser A; A disconnects during a test and the worker obtains browser B. The test continues on B, but its MP4 only contains activity from A, or saving A's replay fails. **Recommended fix:** Track the lease used by the active provider recording and handle worker-scope replacement explicitly, either by stopping and publishing the previous segment and starting another on the new lease, or by failing the attempt instead of claiming a complete replay.

🔴 **Ready label survives a concurrent push** When a push precedes `gh pr edit --add-label`, the workflow skips removal because its event payload lacks the new label. The stale label remains on an unverified head.
Learn more The synchronize event carries a snapshot of labels at the instant GitHub created it. The babysit handoff adds the label independently after a READY snapshot, so a push between its status check and label update can produce an event without the label. The job-level condition skips the only step that reads current labels, leaving the newly applied label on a different head. A synchronize event that did include the label can also remove a label newly applied to a later head if execution is delayed. **Example:** A bot pushes head B after the agent checks head A; the agent labels B's PR using its earlier READY result. B's synchronize event lacked the label at dispatch, so the workflow skips and B remains labeled without verification. **Recommended fix:** Run the drop job on every synchronize event and guard the deletion using a head-to-label association or check the current head against the event head. Ensure the babysit handoff rechecks the head immediately before adding the label, because a post-label snapshot alone cannot make the add atomic.

The second segment begins at 10:00:05 and has no caption until another step starts. **Recommended fix:** Select steps whose time intervals overlap each segment, clamp cue starts to its start and cue ends to the next segment's start, and include the carried-over step on the new segment.

🔴 **Near-miss scoring stalls failed runs** On dense screens, `locatorCandidates` computes full edit-distance matrices for every requested word against every observed word. The web engine permits 3,000 nodes and 512-character text fields, while synchronous scoring ignores the five-second evidence timeout. A failed locator can block the runner long after its deadline.
Learn more Failure evidence is captured under a five-second abort signal, but candidate ranking runs synchronously after the observation returns. [captureFailureEvidence](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/7335f18cc2a116bcbaeae2e8f93c2f662a3079e6/packages/e2e/src/run/failure-evidence.ts#L49-L94 "packages/e2e/src/run/failure-evidence.ts:49-94") does not pass that signal into candidate ranking. Each new [isTypoOf](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/7335f18cc2a116bcbaeae2e8f93c2f662a3079e6/packages/e2e/src/internal/suggest.ts#L29-L30 "packages/e2e/src/internal/suggest.ts:29-30") call constructs a complete edit-distance matrix, even when the candidate has a different role. The web engine can supply up to 3,000 nodes in one observation through [captureObservation](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/7335f18cc2a116bcbaeae2e8f93c2f662a3079e6/packages/web/src/observation-capture.ts#L11-L12 "packages/web/src/observation-capture.ts:11-12"), and a node's text can reach 512 characters. Ranking can therefore continue consuming CPU and memory after the evidence deadline expires. **Example:** A requested single 512-character word and 3,000 buttons with distinct 512-character text words trigger roughly 3,000 matrices with over 260,000 cells each, before the report can finish. **Recommended fix:** Bound `locatorCandidates` work by excluding ineligible roles before word comparisons, rejecting pairs whose length difference exceeds the typo budget, and using a budget-aware, space-bounded distance calculation. Make ranking observe the evidence deadline so expensive diagnostics cannot delay a failed attempt indefinitely.

🔴 **Shared app sessions fail across targets** When targets share a command but declare different services, `declaredProcessesKey` gives them separate process pools. The second session retries the running command and fails with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`.
Learn more The MCP host pools app processes by the digest of the entire target declaration. Two targets can use one app command while declaring different dependencies. Their digests differ, so [SharedAppProcesses](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/7a5fbf4cff9f512884bdbaaf177bf25d5e3c689d/packages/e2e/src/run/provision.ts#L169-L184 "packages/e2e/src/run/provision.ts:169-184") starts the same command twice. [ManagedProcess](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/7a5fbf4cff9f512884bdbaaf177bf25d5e3c689d/packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts#L152-L170 "packages/e2e/src/run/managed-process.ts:152-170") refuses the second start when its readiness URL already answers and `reuseExisting` is false. The second target cannot open, although it could share the existing app process. **Example:** Target `desktop` declares a database service and `pnpm dev` at port 3000; target `mobile-web` declares `pnpm dev` at the same port without that service. Open `desktop`, then open `mobile-web`: the second session fails with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` instead of opening another browser. **Recommended fix:** Track service and command ownership independently, or merge compatible declarations across sessions before provisioning. Reference-count each distinct process and only stop it after its last user leaves; preserve dependency ordering and detect conflicting declarations.

🔴 **Server shutdown abandons in-flight sessions** If the client disconnects during `open_session` or `close_session`, `closeAll` skips sessions outside `live`. An opening session can start an app after shutdown; a closing session can leave its cleanup unfinished.
Learn more The server calls [closeAll](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/7a5fbf4cff9f512884bdbaaf177bf25d5e3c689d/packages/e2e/src/mcp/server.ts#L91-L103 "packages/e2e/src/mcp/server.ts:91-103") when its transport closes. Session IDs enter `opening` before startup and enter `live` only after the attempt and step initialize; [closeLive](https://github.com/tester-army/e2e/blob/7a5fbf4cff9f512884bdbaaf177bf25d5e3c689d/packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts#L143-L154 "packages/e2e/src/mcp/session.ts:143-154") removes an ID from `live` before its asynchronous cleanup completes. Consequently neither operation is awaited by shutdown. An opening session can finish starting a browser or app command after shutdown has run, and an in-progress close can still be disposing resources when shutdown finishes. **Example:** An MCP client sends `open_session` for a slow app and disconnects while it boots. `closeAll` sees an empty `live` map, returns, and the pending open completes with nobody left to close the session. **Recommended fix:** Track opening promises and closing promises. On shutdown, block new opens, cancel or await all openings, then close and await all live and already-closing sessions before closing the transport.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The changeset says junit.xml cannot carry run errors**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

The release note lists "run errors" among the things "that `junit.xml` cannot carry". This is not correct: `renderJunitReport` writes each run-level error as a test case of a synthetic `run` suite (`packages/e2e/src/report/junit.ts:258`), and the PR description says so too ("run-level errors become a made-up `run` suite").

Evidence: on both the base and the head, a run with one passing test and an `afterAll` that throws writes `<testsuite name="run" tests="1" failures="0" errors="1">` to `junit.xml`. The difference between the two formats is how they count run errors, not whether they carry them. The changelog entry that users read describes JUnit incorrectly.

**P3 · Non-blocking · A redirect drops the response that sent it, with no way to opt out**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

`fetch` runs with the default `redirect: 'follow'`, and no option changes it. When a server answers `302 Location: /ok` with `set-cookie: sid=1`, `request.get('/redir')` returns status 200 for `/ok`, and `headers['set-cookie']` is absent: the 302 status, its `location`, and its cookie are lost. I ran this against a loopback server at this head. A sign-in endpoint that redirects after it sets the session cookie has this shape, and the docs tell users to pass that cookie in `headers`. Playwright's `request` has `maxRedirects: 0` for this case, and `docs/reference/request.mdx:95` says only "Redirects are followed".

**P3 · Non-blocking · fetch changes `Accept-Encoding` when the request has a `Range` header**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

The fixture refuses headers that `fetch` sets, drops, or overwrites, but it accepts `Accept-Encoding` with `Range`. In that case `fetch` appends `identity` (the fetch spec's rule for range requests). With `{ range: 'bytes=0-9', 'accept-encoding': 'gzip, identity;q=0' }` the server receives `gzip, identity;q=0, identity`, so the request is not the one the test wrote. Node's own `fetch` does the same, so this is rare, but it is a case of the rule this code states.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The new integration suite never removes its fixture projects**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

No `runProject` call in this file uses the `project` it returns, so no project is removed with `project.cleanup()`. Each run leaves its projects in `tests/tmp-projects/`. Of the 48 integration suites that call `runProject`, this is the only one that never calls `.cleanup()`; the one `cleanup` in it is a test name.

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

The comment says that a push or pull request "runs the same checks as separate steps". The separate steps do not include `docs:check`, which is part of `pnpm check` (`package.json:13`). On a push or pull request, `spec` does not run `docs:check`; the separate `docs.yml` workflow runs it on pull requests and in the merge queue when its path filter matches. The behavior is correct and did not change. Only the comment describes more coverage than the separate steps give, which can mislead the next person who edits this job.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The matrix comment gives the wrong duration for the two halves**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

The comment says "two halves of about seven minutes each". The jobs on this head do not agree:

- `runner`: 7m55s to 8m58s
- `packages`: 5m08s to 5m40s, and 8m16s on 24.8.0

A person who later tunes the split or the timeout reads about 8 minutes of headroom for the `runner` half. The measured headroom is about 6 minutes.

**P2 · Fix before merge · The report-1 schema accepts a `todo` skip on attempts and on results with attempts**

`todo` was added to the skip definition that result, attempt, and serial-member skips share. A report that puts `{ "cause": "todo", "reason": "todo" }` on an attempt, or on a result that has attempts, therefore validates. `docs/reference/test.mdx:146` says a todo test never runs and has no attempts, and the schema is the wire contract that consumers validate against.

Evidence: I took `schema/fixtures/report-v1.valid.json`, changed its result that has a skipped attempt to `status: skipped` with the `todo` skip on the result and on the attempt, and validated it with Ajv 2020 against the schema at this head. It was accepted. No negative fixture covers this shape.

Then the job stopped near `@e2e-dev/notte` with `The operation was canceled.`, so the root `test` script did not start the later packages (lightpanda, eas, smol, acp, testmu, and others).
- A reader can take "so 15 cancelled jobs" to mean fifteen jobs, not a 15-minute limit that cancelled jobs.

**P2 · Fix before merge · A worker fixture in a module that registers a hook gets one instance per test file, also without parallel runs**

When a module declares a worker fixture and also registers a hook (for example a `fixtures.ts` with `test.extend` and a `test.beforeEach`), the module is now a registrar. Each test file then evaluates it again with its own `?e2e=` key. Each evaluation creates a new `FixtureDefinition`, and `WorkerFixturePool` keys its instances by that definition (`packages/e2e/src/run/fixture-pool.ts:141`). The result is one setup per test file on each worker. All instances stay live until the worker exits.

This applies to every project on Node.js, also when no file sets `parallel` or `fullyParallel`.

Evidence: one worker, two test files that import such a `fixtures.ts`:

- main: `setup, hook, body a, body b, teardown` (the hook is missing for file b, which is the bug that this pull request fixes)
- head: `setup, hook, body a, setup, hook, body b, teardown, teardown`

A worker fixture that holds an exclusive resource (a fixed port, a per-worker database, a server process) fails or leaks on the second instance. `docs/reference/test.mdx` narrows the worker fixture sentence, but `.changeset/imported-registrations.md` does not mention the change, so users get no warning in the release notes.

**P2 · Fix before merge · A realm retired before a serial group is reused after a later test in the unit fails**

Before a serial group runs, `runFileUnit` calls `this.realms.retire(realm)`, which puts the realm in `reusable` for the file. If a later ordinary test in the same unit fails, its realm is dropped, but the earlier entry stays in `reusable`. The next unit of the same file on that worker then gets that realm from `takeReusable`, which holds the module state of the tests before the serial group.

This breaks the rule of this pull request that a unit with a failed test does not hand its import to the next unit.

Reproduction (one worker, one file): an ordinary test that passes and changes module state, then a serial group, then an ordinary test that fails, then a parallel test that expects clean module state.

- main: all 4 tests pass
- head: the last test fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED: expected 1 to be 0`

**P2 · Fix before merge · Parallel repeats record the replay cache live instead of replaying the first run**

`splitFile` keys each parallel scope and each hooked run by agent and repeat, so with `--repeat-each` the repeats of one test become separate units. On two or more workers, they start at the same time. With an empty cache, every repeat calls the model and saves its own recording.

`docs/reference/cli.mdx:730` says: "With the replay cache on, the first run records and the rest replay."

Evidence: `--repeat-each 2`, two workers, empty cache, a parallel file with one `agent.act` step.

- main: repeat 0 records, repeat 1 replays
- head: both repeats call the model and both are `saved`

The verdicts are correct, but the run costs one model call per repeat, and the docs promise otherwise.

**P2 · Fix before merge · A dynamic import of a registrar from a shared utility returns the first test file's instance**

`inFreshLoad` takes the key from the parent URL or from `importing.at(-1)`. A utility module that is not a registrar is not re-evaluated, so it has no `?e2e=` key. When that utility calls `import('./helper.ts')` from a test body, after collection, `importing` is empty and the resolution keeps the plain URL. The import then returns the instance of the first test file that loaded `helper.ts`.

In the second test file, the helper from the static import and the helper from the dynamic import are different objects, with different module state.

Evidence: an identity check between the two imports in the second file passes on main and fails on head. This pattern is rare.

Three Chrome rules for role acceptance are not copied. In each case, the header inside the element reads as `banner` on this head, but Chrome reads `sectionheader`. On main, the reader does not read it as `banner`.

| Input (with a `<header>` inside) | main | this head | Chrome |

**P2 · Fix before merge · The keyboard hint replaces a correct hint when the refusal has another cause**

`keyboardCut` checks only `viewport.height < screen.height`. It does not check why agent-device refused the point, so the keyboard hint also replaces agent-device's own hint in these cases:

- **Edge or off-screen point while the keyboard is open.** On a 402x874 screen with the keyboard viewport cut to 402x590, an untimed swipe that refuses at `(0, 400)` (agent-device requires a 1-point inset) or at `(603, 1800)` (screenshot pixels instead of points) gets "pass duration to send the path as given, across the keyboard". A timed pan is refused for the same point, so this advice does not help. The correct hint ("Move the gesture away from the edge" or "Use the coordinate units snapshot reports") is lost. On the base, those cases keep agent-device's hint. This also contradicts the PR description: "An off-screen path, or a timed swipe, keeps agent-device's own hint".
- **Stale screen size after a rotation.** `device.setOrientation()` takes no snapshot, so `knownViewport` keeps the portrait size (390x844) until the next observation. After `setOrientation('landscape')`, an untimed swipe off the 844x390 landscape viewport gets the keyboard hint with no keyboard open.

Evidence: I called `refusedSwipePath` directly with these inputs, and all three cases returned the keyboard hint. agent-device 0.21.42 puts the refused point in `details.sample.point`, and the viewport keeps the full screen width when the keyboard cuts it. Both values are available to make the check exact.

If a test focuses a field (or the app autofocuses one at launch) and then calls `screen.swipe` with numeric points before any observation, the swipe that crosses the keyboard is refused, but the message keeps agent-device's coordinate-units hint, not the `duration` hint. The error code is `NOT_ACTIONABLE` as intended. Only the hint is missing.

The new test calls `observed(h, 'About')` before every case, so it does not cover this path. A test without a prior observation would show it.

**P1 · Blocking · A shard stopped by --max-failures or --max-duration merges as interrupted (exit 130)**

`--max-failures` and `--max-duration` can stop a run while other tests are still active. Those tests end `interrupted`, and the shard exits 1 (`docs/reference/cli.mdx:728-729`: "Exits 1 ... not 130"). This line sets 130 when any result is `interrupted`, and `combineExitCodes` on line 172 ranks 130 above 1. As a result, the merged run reports `interrupted` with exit 130, even for a one-shard merge.

Reproduced with the built CLI:

- `run --shard 1/1 --max-failures 1` with `workers: 2`, one failing test and one slow test: the shard reports `failed`, exit 1. `merge-reports shard-1` reports `interrupted`, exit 130.
- `run --shard 1/1 --max-duration 1500` with one 8 s test: the shard reports `failed`, exit 1. The merge reports `interrupted`, exit 130.

The new reference page says that a per-shard `--max-failures` stop "keeps its failing verdict". The existing test covers this case only with `workers: 1`, where nothing is interrupted. CI treats 130 as a cancellation, so the merged job shows the wrong outcome.

**P2 · Fix before merge · Shards that use a free app port (http://127.0.0.1:0) cannot be merged**

The target comparison includes `baseOrigin`. With the documented free-port declaration (`url: 'http://127.0.0.1:0'`, `docs/reference/config.mdx` "Free ports"), each shard gets a port when its config loads. The origin is therefore different in each shard, although the declaration is the same.

Reproduced: two passing shards recorded `http://127.0.0.1:65425` and `http://127.0.0.1:65434`. `merge-reports shard-1 shard-2` exited 2 with `shard 2 has different targets`. The same project with a fixed port merged without errors.

For these projects, the merge fails every time.

**P2 · Fix before merge · A merge config in a subdirectory gives reporters the wrong projectRoot**

`docs/ci.mdx` recommends a separate `--config` for publishers such as `github()` in the merge job, and it describes a merge config in a subdirectory. In that case, `discovered.projectRoot` is the directory of that config. The paths in the report (`result.file`) are relative to the project that ran the tests.

Reproduced with `merge-reports shard-1 --config ci/merge.config.mjs --output <abs>`: the reporter received `projectRoot = <project>/ci`, and `file = tests/a.e2e.ts`. `@e2e-dev/github` builds source links from `run.projectRoot` (`packages/github/src/reporter.ts:186`). Its links then point to `ci/tests/a.e2e.ts`, which does not exist. The trace paths in `traces` (line 68) are computed from the same root.

**P2 · Fix before merge · A shard with no recorded commit fails the merge as "a different commit"**

`detectVcs` asks git with a one-second budget and leaves `run.vcs` undefined when git does not answer in time. Outside GitHub Actions there is no `GITHUB_SHA` fallback. `packages/e2e/src/internal/vcs.ts` says "Nothing here fails a run". This line compares `undefined` with the sha of the other shard and throws `shard N has a different commit`. One slow git call on a loaded runner therefore fails the merge of valid shards with a misleading message.

An independent run reproduced it: a `git` shim that sleeps 2 s, used for shard 2 only, made `merge-reports` exit 2 with that message. Without the shim, the merge exited 0. The same reviewer saw the new test "keeps both shared setup executions..." fail once with this error when the whole file ran under load. The test passed when it ran alone.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The merged output directory is created with mode 0700**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

`mkdtemp` always creates a directory with mode 0700, and the `rename` on line 71 publishes that directory as `--output`. Reproduced: the merged directory has mode `40700`, while the shard output directories and a normal `e2e run` output have mode 755. A later step that runs as another user cannot read the merged report. Examples are a container step that runs as root followed by a host step, or a separate publishing user.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The merged report drops run.filters and run.changes, so summaries lose the Change and Filter lines**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

Each shard's `changes` and `filters` go only into `extensions['e2e.merge'].shards[]`. `run.changes` and `run.filters` stay unset on the merged run. The markdown reporter (`filtersSection` in `packages/e2e/src/report/markdown.ts`) and `@e2e-dev/github` read those fields. Because no reporter reads the extension, a merged PR comment shows the left-out table but no `**Change**` or `**Filter**` lines. An independent run showed that an unsharded `run --changed-since main` with a config filter prints both lines, and the 2-shard merge of the same run prints neither line. The reference page documents that the data goes to the extension. However, the merged report is presented as the one report for the matrix, and the data is lost to every reporter.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The target check ignores engine identity and capabilities, but the first shard's target record is used for all shards**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

`checkRun` compares target id, platform, environment, and origin. It does not compare the engine name, version, SPI version, or capabilities. The merged run then publishes `first.targets` for every result. An independent run merged one shard with the engine's state capability off and one with it on. The merge produced only a config-digest warning, exited 0, and published `stateCapability: false` for both shards. The trigger is uncommon, because shards normally share the lockfile. **P3 · Non-blocking · Ctrl-C in a filter prompt leaves the active prompt line on screen**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

**Trigger:** in `e2e run --watch` in a terminal, press `p` or `t`, then press Ctrl-C.

**Cause:** the Ctrl-C keypress goes to the listeners in this order:

1. `Keyboard`'s interrupt-only listener, which `pause()` adds before clack adds its listener. It calls `signals.escalate()`, and `close` aborts `closer`.
2. clack's abort handler calls `close()`. This writes a newline but does not render the prompt again.
3. clack's own keypress listener gets the same Ctrl-C, because `EventEmitter` copies the listener list before it emits. It renders the cancel frame and closes the prompt again.

The newline from step 2 moved the cursor down one line, so the redraw in step 3 does not cover the active line.

**Evidence:** built CLI in a 120x40 pty: press `p`, wait for the prompt, then send `\x03`. The screen was rendered from the captured bytes.

- main: `■  Filter by a file name, path, or glob (empty clears the filter)`
- this PR: `◆  Filter by a file name, …` and below it `■  Filter by a file name, …`

On this PR, the bytes after Ctrl-C start with `\r\n\x1b[?25h` before the cancel frame. On main, the cancel frame comes first. The unit test does not show this, because the mocked prompt has no keypress listener.

The CLI handles `--reporter json` in non-quiet mode and redirects stdout to stderr before config loading. Quiet mode is used by the public SDK and that does not expose the CLI reporter override.

The existing integration tests cover:
- A configured list reporter overridden by `--reporter json` in the CLI.
- Configured JSON reporters in quiet mode.

I considered this and verified the behavior (on both main and this branch) when an invalid byte arrives in the same write or a subsequent write. In both cases, the replacement character is delivered to the reporter. The implementation intentionally lets `StringDecoder` handle sequences with continuation bytes. Assigning individual replacement characters to their originating writes would increase complexity without addressing an existing regression.

On main the same config created `buyer` with the default options and the run passed.

The PR body and the changeset describe this change. But the stability policy in `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("What is covered": config keys, their types, and their defaults) says that a breaking change to a covered surface ships with a deprecation first, and the changeset bumps it as a `patch`. AGENTS.md also says that a breaking change is a `minor` whose summary opens with `**Breaking:**`.

The motivating case `ci ? { buyer } : {}` does not depend on this skip: at runtime the object has no `buyer` key when the condition is false. Only an explicit `undefined` value reaches this line.

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

The getter returns `getErrors()[0]`, and `AttemptVerdict.errors()` returns the primary error followed by the secondary errors. When the attempt has only secondary errors (for example a cleanup error), `testInfo.error` is that secondary error. `TestInfo.error` is documented as the primary error, or `undefined` if none (`packages/core/src/types/test-info.ts`).

**P3 · Non-blocking · result.annotations reads the last attempt, not the verdict attempt**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

`resultAnnotations()` uses `result.attempts.at(-1)`. When the run interrupts a retry, the result's verdict comes from the earlier failed attempt, but its `annotations` come from the interrupted retry. Runtime annotations that differ between attempts are then shown on the wrong verdict. `ReportResult.annotations` is documented as coming from the last verdict attempt, and the list reporter already selects the earlier attempt.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The list reporter hides runtime annotations of a serial member that skipped itself**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

`neverRan` is `true` for every skipped member, so a member that pushed an annotation and then called `test.skip()` shows only its declared annotations in `list`. `report.json` shows the runtime annotation for the same member. `memberRan()` in `packages/core/src/run/records.ts:255` already separates a self-skip from a runner skip.

**P3 · Non-blocking · The in-process guard rejects runs whose attempts do not overlap**

_Optional. This does not block the merge._

`liveInProcessRunners` is module-wide, so it counts runners of all programmatic runs in the process, not only of one run. When one `run()` with an inline config is still in engine `init` and a second one starts, the second exits with `WORKER_PROTOCOL`, although neither run has published an attempt yet. On main, both runs pass in the same sequence.
